newsitem.title: USA: Israel leader to approve housing plan - Jerusalem mayor.
newsitem.headline: Israel leader to approve housing plan - Jerusalem mayor.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu next week will approve construction of a controversial housing project in Jerusalem, Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert said on Wednesday.

"I want to reassure you that next week, the Israeli cabinet will approve of a plan to build a new neighbourhood in the south part of Jerusalem, in the section called Har Homa," Olmert said in a speech at a Jewish temple.

The New York Times reported earlier on Wednesday that the issue posed a dilemma for Netanyahu, since approving the plan was likely to rile the Palestinians, while backing down would anger right-wing members of Netanyahu's coalition.
Har Homa is in East Jerusalem, south of the Old City, on land conquered by Israel in 1967.
Olmert, a member of Netanyahu's Likud Party, said he spoke to the premier on the telephone earlier on Wednesday.

"We have to do what we have to do," Olmert said. "Whether people agree or do not agree. Whether they like it, whether they don't like it, as long as we are certain that this is the right thing for Jerusalem."
"Because it will always be at the wrong time for those who don't like us to be there in the first place," he said.
"We will build 7,000 new units on land which was expropriated first and foremost from the Jews," he said.
Olmert was in the United States on a fundraising trip for a children's rehabilitation centre in Jerusalem. He will return to Israel on Thursday.
